lane: SEVER_BOND cheat vector — construct the case for an owner ruling (READ-ONLY probe, no files touched)
summary: The vector is REAL and still live at commit 7d1514b. `SEVER_BOND` is a CLIENT INTENT (`protocol.ts:1545`), and the host's intent pipeline re-derives exactly ONE field — `playerId`, via `stampOrReject` (`intentStamp.ts:37-39`). `bondId` and `cause` cross the wire and are trusted verbatim. `canSeverBond` (`disruptionManager.ts:81-101`) returns `true` unconditionally for seven of the eight `cause` values, so a modified peer sending `{type:'SEVER_BOND', bondId:<any bond on the snapshot>, cause:'physics'}` gets an unconditional, currency-free deletion of any connector in the world — no disruption charge, no raid point, no accumulated damage, no enemy check, and `severActor` returns `undefined` for `'physics'` (`severBond.ts:149-150`) so the victim's sever toast names nobody. The handoff's one-line description is accurate in every particular. TWO things collapse the severity, and both must be in the brief: (1) the bench/elimination gate in `dispatch()` (`world.ts:500`, `world.ts:524`) blocks EVERY `SEVER_BOND` from a benched or eliminated seat regardless of cause, so this is a live-seat cheat, not a dead-seat kingmaker; (2) the honest client no longer sends `SEVER_BOND` AT ALL — `grep -n "type: 'SEVER_BOND'" src` returns zero non-test hits outside the sim's own reducers, because S152/S168 rewired the RMB arm to `RAID_TARGET` (`controls.ts:1201-1204`). That second fact is what makes the fix nearly free: the host can hard-override `cause` at one choke point and no honest player can tell.

findings.claim: The bypass arm is literally unconditional and currency-free for seven of the eight cause values — the handoff's description is verified, not refuted.

findings.claim: The wire validator checks only that `action.type` is a known discriminant. No payload field of any action is shape-checked — `cause` and `bondId` are passed through as whatever the peer sent.

The host's only re-derivation is playerId. `stampSenderSeat` spreads the action and replaces exactly one key — `cause` survives untouched. This is the single choke point both host paths use, which is also why it is the right place to fix it.

Host INTENT apply path: rate-limit -> type allowlist -> seat stamp -> dispatch. There is no fourth gate. (The migration successor at main.ts:3473-3489 is byte-for-byte the same three gates, and also routes through stampOrReject.)
The reducer applies it with no ownership or enemy check of any kind — unlike the RAID_TARGET arm, which does have one. Any bondId that resolves is severed.
REACHABILITY CONFIRMED, not blocked: bond ids ride the NetSnapshot, so a joiner already knows every bond id in the host's world, including the host's own towers.

SEVERITY COLLAPSE #1 (must be in the brief): the dispatch()-level bench and elimination gates block SEVER_BOND for a benched or eliminated seat REGARDLESS of cause, because they key on action.type + playerId. The exploit therefore requires a live, un-benched seat. It is not a dead-seat kingmaker.

SEVERITY COLLAPSE #2, and the key to a free fix: NO production client path dispatches SEVER_BOND. The RMB bond arm was rewired to RAID_TARGET in S152/S168, so the honest client never puts SEVER_BOND on the wire at all. Every remaining dispatcher is host-side sim code (physicsLoop, creatureAttack, suicideBlast, droneLifecycle, voltkinChain, bombLifecycle, the RAID_TARGET reducer).

THEFT, on the one stat ladder: a spoofed sever skips the entire structure-wide pool. structurePoolFifths(n) = n×(5+n) — 50/36/24/14/6 — and damageConnector only returns true once banked damage reaches it. The cheat pays zero fifths.

THEFT, priced against the honest raid: one raid point buys 3 fifths (capped), MAX_RAID_POINTS is 3, and a raid point costs 10 raid progress (5 per tower built / 2 per connection). So the first connector of a 5-connector tower = 50 fifths = 17 raid points = 170 raid progress. The whole tower (130 fifths) = 44 raid points = 440 progress. The cheat does it in 1 and 5 intents respectively.

TESTS (item 6): the bypass arm IS pinned as correct — but only at the PURE HELPER, never at the network boundary. Every assertion hand-builds the action and calls canSeverBond/applySeverBond directly. A host-side cause-normalisation fix therefore turns NONE of them red.

TESTS: fix shape (b) — 'make the bypass arm pay' — would turn at least six assertions red AND re-break a shipped bug the code explicitly records. The bypass is the sim's own re-dispatch contract, not a player convenience.

TESTS: fix shape (c) — removing SEVER_BOND from the allowlist — is NOT a one-line change. Two set-equality tests force the bench and elimination policy rows to be deleted with it, and deleting those rows RE-ARMS a benched or eliminated seat's already-spawned creatures to sever connectors (see the world.ts:500/524 gates above). That is a live gameplay change needing its own ruling.

fix_shape:
RECOMMENDED — fix (a), host re-derives `cause` and ignores the client's, at the ONE choke point.

`src/net/intentStamp.ts` — extend `stampOrReject` (line 37) / `stampSenderSeat` (line 23) so a `SEVER_BOND` arriving from the wire has its `cause` forced to `'player'` as well as its `playerId` forced to the sender's seat. ~6 lines of code + a docblock in the house style. This covers BOTH host apply paths — `hostHandlers.ts:337` and the migration successor at `main.ts:3477` — because `grep -rn "stampOrReject" src` returns exactly those two call sites and nothing else. Nothing else in the repo calls `stampSenderSeat` except `stampOrReject` itself and `nplayerSeating.test.ts`.

Why `'player'` and not "drop the intent": `'player'` is the only cause a peer could ever legitimately claim, and it routes straight into the existing hostile-auth + disruption-charge gate at `disruptionManager.ts:103-112`. The cheat becomes the honest, priced action.

Cost: 1 production file, 1 test file. No behaviour any honest player can observe, because no production client path dispatches `SEVER_BOND` at all (verified: `grep -n "type: 'SEVER_BOND'" src --include=*.ts` has zero non-test hits outside host-side sim reducers; `controls.ts`'s RMB bond arm emits `RAID_TARGET`).

REFUTED — fix (b), "make the bypass arm require the same currency". Do NOT do this. The bypass is not a loophole, it is the contract every in-sim severer depends on: `creatureAttack.ts:571`, `suicideBlast.ts:182`, `droneLifecycle.ts:218`, `voltkinChain.ts:262`, `bombLifecycle.ts:146`, `physicsLoop.ts:244`, and the `RAID_TARGET` reducer at `world.ts:776`. Charging them re-creates the exact bug recorded at `disruptionManager.ts:97-99` — a fully-damaged connector silently refusing to break — and turns red at minimum `disruptionManager.test.ts:114, 147, 205-211, 239-243` and `severBond.test.ts:103`.

OPTIONAL, NOT FREE — fix (c), remove `SEVER_BOND: true` from `CLIENT_INTENT_TYPES_RECORD` (`protocol.ts:1545`). Correct in principle (no honest client sends it) and it closes the vector at the outermost boundary, but it drags in `benchGate.ts:55` and `elimination.ts:81` via the two set-equality tests, and deleting those rows re-arms a benched/eliminated seat's creatures to cut connectors. Only take this if the owner wants that second question opened. It composes cleanly on top of (a) later; it is not a prerequisite.
four_sites_risk: NONE. `cause` lives on the ACTION union (`world.ts:233`), not on a hashed entity — there is no factory, no serialize, no hash contribution and no worker projection for it. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 47 (`protocol.ts:704`): nothing is added to or removed from the wire, the host simply stops trusting a field it already receives, and a stale peer's HELLO is refused at handshake regardless. Determinism is untouched — the normalisation runs on the host BEFORE `dispatch`, so the direct path (`dispatch(deps.world, action)`) and the worker path (`deps.dispatchAction(action)`) at `hostHandlers.ts:344-345` both receive the identical already-stamped action, and the migration successor gets it through the same helper. The one thing to keep in view: the fix must live in `intentStamp.ts`, NOT be open-coded at either call site — `main.ts:3477` is the successor path that S143 already had to repair once for exactly this "two apply paths, one of them forgotten" reason.
tests_owed:
Nothing existing goes red under fix (a) — verified: there is no `src/net/intentStamp.test.ts`; the stamp helper's tests live in `src/state/nplayerSeating.test.ts:271-288` and none of them mention `SEVER_BOND`.

Owed, and following the S182 lesson that a source-text guard proves a line EXISTS but not that it is REACHED:
1. In the `stampSenderSeat` describe block (`nplayerSeating.test.ts:271`): a wire action `{type:'SEVER_BOND', bondId, playerId: <other seat>, cause:'physics'}` stamped for seat 2 must come back with `playerId === 2` AND `cause === 'player'`.
2. A MECHANICAL enumeration rather than prose: assert that the set of `cause` values the host will accept from the wire is exactly `{'player'}` — drive `stampOrReject` over a literal array of all eight union members pinned by a `satisfies SeverBondAction['cause'][]` so adding a ninth cause fails `tsc` until someone decides it. That is the "count the fills and pin the total" pattern from the S182 placement branch, with teeth.
3. One end-to-end assertion at the reducer, not the helper: build a real 5-connector component, dispatch the normalised action for a 0-charge attacker, and assert the bond HOLDS — the current suite only ever asserts the bypass works, never that a wire-shaped physics claim is refused.
4. Optional but cheap: assert `world.diagnostics` counts the normalisation (or leave it silent by design and say so) — a silent rewrite is indistinguishable from a bug in a bug report.
owner_questions: Take the Micro fix (host forces `cause:'player'` on any wire SEVER_BOND), or leave the vector open under the repo's own stated friends-only threat model? The case for taking it: one file, ~6 lines, no PROTOCOL bump, no test goes red, and zero honest players notice because no production client sends SEVER_BOND at all any more. The case for leaving it: `protocol.ts:1445/1452/1478` repeatedly rationalise wire-allowing host-internal actions as 'inert under the friends-only model', and this is the same argument — though `protocol.ts:1487` already records a session deciding to 'rely on that gate rather than the inert-under-friends-only rationalization'.

Separate and genuinely yours: should a BENCHED or ELIMINATED seat's already-spawned creatures still be able to cut connectors? Today they CANNOT — `world.ts:500/524` blocks every SEVER_BOND whose playerId is a benched/dead seat, whatever the cause, purely as a side effect of SEVER_BOND sitting on the client-intent allowlist. Closing the allowlist (fix c) would re-arm them. The recommended fix (a) leaves this exactly as it is and does not need an answer; this only needs a ruling if you also want fix (c).
size_estimate: Micro (<10K tokens, 2 files) — `src/net/intentStamp.ts` plus assertions in `src/state/nplayerSeating.test.ts`. The whole change is one field normalisation at a single choke point with no wire, hash or worker consequence; the deliberation weight is in the owner's yes/no, not in the edit. If he also wants fix (c), it becomes Standard (5 files, two policy tables, four test edits, and a gameplay ruling attached).
